## Design

### 2026-10-10 – I decided on making a thin portable macro-pad with the ability to use multiple button presses together to make new outputs. Research on integrated circuits to find capacitive touch sensors to be the b

**2h**

I decided on making a thin portable macro-pad with the ability to use multiple button presses together to make new outputs. Research on integrated circuits to find capacitive touch sensors to be the best fit for the project to allow a slimmer profile in comparison to mechanical keyboard switches.  Taking understanding from the TTP 223 module and the official IC documentation to determine all IC's required to build.

### 2026-10-10 – I continued research into the touch/proximity sensors to find out how the conductive pad works and the ways I could wire the sensors to the Xiao Seeed. I thought at first to wire them via a key matrix

**2h**

I continued research into the touch/proximity sensors to find out how the conductive pad works and the ways I could wire the sensors to the Xiao Seeed. I thought at first to wire them via a key matrix with diodes but since I want to use multiple key presses at the same time, I need to make them a direct connection to their own pin. I found out that really its only resistors and capacitors need to dial in the sensitivity and that I could use a 2-layer pcb to have one layer be the signal layer and the other hol

### 2026-10-11 – I worked on the basic schematic of all the IC and capacitors for the 3x3 pad.  The mode pin wired to high constantly to set it to fast mode for a better latency. The output is connected to its own gpi

**3h**

I worked on the basic schematic of all the IC and capacitors for the 3x3 pad.  The mode pin wired to high constantly to set it to fast mode for a better latency. The output is connected to its own gpio pin on the XIAO and the 1 and 8 pin hooked together preparing for the exposed copper padding. Other misclenous power pins hooked up according to the IC's datasheet.
